title: Size bound for tree-unrolling
statement: Let $F$ be a layered Boolean circuit with input nodes indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and output type $\mathrm{out}$. Designate each non-input node as AND or OR, and suppose every gate has finite arity. If there is a natural number $k$ such that every gate has at most $k$ inputs, then for every output node $o$, the tree circuit obtained by unrolling $o$ has size at most $(k+1)^{\mathrm{depth}(F)}$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a layered Boolean circuit from $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ to $\mathrm{out}$
Each non-input node has an AND-or-OR designation
$k$ is a natural number bounding every gate's arity
replaced:
Let $F$ be a layered feedforward circuit over the Boolean alphabet with input type
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and output type $\mathrm{out}$, of depth $d$, in which each gate is
designated an AND gate or an OR gate. Suppose every gate has finite input arity, and
that there is a bound $k \in \bbn$ such that every gate reads from at most $k$ input
wires. Then for each output node $o$, the tree-unrolled Boolean circuit obtained from
$o$ has size (its total number of AND/OR gates and literal leaves) at most $(k+1)^{d}$.
